description:
Here are the descriptions of the line plots, following your guidelines:

The plot illustrates the relationship between iteration number and loss for several language models. The x-axis is labeled “#Iteration” and is a linear scale ranging from 0 to 140000, with tick labels at intervals of 20000. The y-axis is labeled “Loss” and is a linear scale ranging from 2.4 to 3.4, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. 

The first line, colored purple and labeled “Vanilla (n=64)”, begins at approximately 3.3 at an iteration of 0 and decreases to approximately 2.85 at an iteration of 140000, exhibiting a rapid decline in the first 20000 iterations, then leveling off. The second line, colored blue and labeled “StrmLLM (n=64, H)", starts at approximately 3.2 at an iteration of 0 and decreases to approximately 2.8 at an iteration of 140000, showing a similar pattern of initial decline and leveling off. The third line, colored orange and labeled “SepLLM (n=64, H)", begins at approximately 3.15 at an iteration of 0 and decreases to approximately 2.75 at an iteration of 140000, also with a similar trend. The fourth line, colored green and labeled “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)", starts at approximately 3.1 at an iteration of 0 and decreases to approximately 2.7 at an iteration of 140000, following a similar pattern. Finally, the fifth line, colored red and labeled “SepLLM (n=128)", begins at approximately 3.1 at an iteration of 0 and decreases to approximately 2.7 at an iteration of 140000, exhibiting a similar trend to the other lines.
